article_title: South Africa's Sharpeville massacre survivors start legal fight for justice and compensation

tasks.prompt: What is the article mainly about?
options: A plan to rebuild every road in Sharpeville
A new inquiry into whether the protest occurred
Survivors and relatives challenging an apartheid-era indemnity law to seek justice and reparations
A trial that convicted police immediately after the massacre
tasks.correct_answer: Survivors and relatives challenging an apartheid-era indemnity law to seek justice and reparations
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה עוסקת במאבק לביטול חוק חסינות מתקופת האפרטהייד כדי לאפשר צדק ופיצויים.

tasks.prompt: What were the protesters demonstrating against in March 1960?
options: Pass laws restricting black people's movement
Closure of the cemetery
Creation of the TRC
A ban on foreign law firms
tasks.correct_answer: Pass laws restricting black people's movement
tasks.explanation_hebrew: המפגינים מחו נגד חוקי המעבר שחייבו שחורים לשאת פנקס והגבילו את תנועתם.

tasks.prompt: What did the 1961 Indemnity Act protect police and government from?
options: Foreign newspaper criticism
Road maintenance duties
Criminal charges and civil claims related to Sharpeville
TRC testimony
tasks.correct_answer: Criminal charges and civil claims related to Sharpeville
tasks.explanation_hebrew: החוק הגן על המשטרה והממשלה מאישומים פליליים ומתביעות אזרחיות הקשורות לטבח.

tasks.prompt: Why can the old law still be challenged against today's state?
options: The constitution erased every old law
Only post-1994 laws can be reviewed
There is no continuity between states
State continuity kept laws in force until repealed, abolished or changed
tasks.correct_answer: State continuity kept laws in force until repealed, abolished or changed
tasks.explanation_hebrew: עקרון רציפות המדינה משאיר חוקים קודמים בתוקף עד ביטולם או שינויים.

tasks.prompt: What does “redress” mean in this context?
options: A formal effort to remedy or compensate for a past wrong
A passbook rule
The clothing of protesters
Preserving every old law
tasks.correct_answer: A formal effort to remedy or compensate for a past wrong
tasks.explanation_hebrew: redress הוא תיקון עוול באמצעות הכרה, סעד או פיצוי.

tasks.prompt: What does it mean that the Act “remains on the statute books”?
options: It appears only in textbooks
It has many translations
It is already unconstitutional
It still formally exists in the country's legislation
tasks.correct_answer: It still formally exists in the country's legislation
tasks.explanation_hebrew: statute books הם אוסף החוקים התקפים, ולכן הביטוי אומר שהחוק עדיין קיים רשמית.

tasks.prompt: Trace the key events from the 1960 protest to the current legal challenge.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג רצף כרונולוגי של לפחות שישה שלבים.
expected_points: Thousands protested pass laws on 21 March 1960
Police opened fire
At least 69 died and more than 200 were injured
The Indemnity Act passed in 1961
It blocked criminal and civil claims
The democratic constitution took effect in 1994
The TRC investigated apartheid crimes
No police officers sought amnesty for Sharpeville
Lawyers filed a High Court constitutional challenge
They also seek class-action certification

tasks.prompt: Why do survivors say the Truth and Reconciliation Commission did not deliver complete justice?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר את תרומת ה־TRC לצד מגבלותיה במקרה Sharpeville.
expected_points: The TRC investigated crimes and brought victims and perpetrators together
Amnesty depended on disclosure and other conditions
Some offenders were not jailed
No police applied for Sharpeville amnesty
The Indemnity Act continued to block proceedings
Survivors say long-term harm remains unremedied
Not all victims were identified for support
They now seek collective remedies and accountability

tasks.prompt: Summarise the massacre, its continuing impact and the goals of the new court case.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לסכם בכבוד את האירוע, החוק, מצב הקהילה והסעדים המבוקשים בלי לנבא את פסק הדין.
expected_points: The protest opposed racist pass laws
Police fired on peaceful demonstrators
At least 69 died and more than 200 were injured
Survivors still carry physical and emotional injuries
The 1961 Act blocked charges and claims
The law remains formally in force
Applicants argue it violates the 1994 constitution
They seek a class action, damages and reparations
Possible criminal cases depend on future legal outcomes
The action seeks justice and healing

tasks.prompt: Write a balanced explainer of what the High Court is being asked to decide and why it matters.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב באנגלית באופן ברור, להבחין בין עובדות, טענות ותוצאות אפשריות ולא לקבוע מראש את הפסיקה.
expected_points: Identify the Indemnity Act and its protections
Explain the constitutional challenge
Describe state continuity
Explain class-action certification
Identify survivors and relatives
Distinguish individual damages from community reparations
Present criminal charges only as a possibility
Mention the government's position on legal remedies
Explain the importance of healing and reform
Do not guarantee compensation or convictions
